My independent band scan reproduces every value. FVS (m): 0.14/1.34/2.05/0.96/0.26/0.00/0.06/0.34/0.82/1.07/1.50/1.02/0.49/0.01/0.23/0.22. Internal solid infill (ISI) values also match. Totals (analisar_gcode.py): FVS 4m15s, 10505 mm, 697 mm³; ISI 2m32s, 4879 mm, 309 mm³. FVS appears at Z 19.56, then not again until 26.44. Line 16367 is Z 2.6, 126107 is Z 15.88, 213988 is Z 30.6.

In evst_arachne_ft.json, slowed layers in bands 4-16 and 32-48 = 0, 16-28 = 47, 52-64 = 18. The count is wrong: those bands hold 175 layers, not 125. Headroom: minimum nominal layer time is 9.7 s at Z 4-8 and 11+ s elsewhere. Removing about 1-1.8 s/layer keeps them above 8 s, though Z 4-8 gets close. This rests on the user's planner, not Bambu's CoolingBuffer. It is irrelevant for 4-up.

My scan gives 2562 FVS extrusion starts preceded by travel, 153 of them with a retraction, over 31.7 m of travel. The 125 s figure comes from the user's planner, so I rate it medium confidence. This planner overestimated the 4-up plate by about 47 min against Bambu Studio (ETAPA_B.md:101).

evst_sim2.json band totals: enabled 1123.9 mm³ against G-code FVS+ISI+Bridge 1035.5. Bands match within about 10-15% (8-12: 160.6 vs 142.9; 40-44: 111.8 vs 100.9; 52-56: 42.3 vs 43.5). This validates only the enabled branch. The partial branch relies on things the simulation simplifies: stTop has no opening (ext_w/10) and no +0.019 mm expansion (PrintObject.cpp:1509,1530,1767), and the second clause of the area filter is omitted.

The simulation output is reported correctly (partial 282.8, partial_nf 330.5). My independent face-slope estimate of the same code geometry also gives about 74% removal overall. It differs by band, though: it keeps about 20-25% of the solid at Z 40-48 and 25-45% at Z 8-16 (40-48° faces keep a ribbon of 7s-0.756 up to about 0.58 mm). So 'Z 12-48 drops to ~0' is not assured. Removal could be roughly 550-775 mm³.

My mesh histogram reproduces the face areas exactly: UP 40-75° = 1653.2 mm² of 6066; Z 32-48 676.6; Z 8-24 408.3; Z 48-56 168.5; UP <12° 33.1 mm². It also finds 370 mm² of 12-40° upward faces and 176 mm² of 40-75° faces at Z 56-65, which the claim leaves out. The 'quarter behind overhangs' share is a simulation result.

The geometry checks out: infill boundary 0.756 mm = wall 0.819 - 15% x 0.416 overlap (PerimeterGenerator.cpp:1465-1471); enabled ribbon 6s; partial strip [0.756, 7s] needs 7s > 1.02, i.e. α < 47.7°. One caveat: for slopes steeper than about 21° (s < 0.42), the visible exterior is the outer wall in both modes. The ribbon only backs the inner walls of the layers above, so a lower perpendicular thickness is not by itself a show-through mechanism.
combine_shells(cache.top_surfaces) at :1947 runs in both modes, so the 6-layer top projection is kept. The G-code has 0.08 m of Top surface. Near-flat upward faces total 33.1 mm².

The direction (shorter) is certain, but the size depends on the simulation. Applying my band-wise analytic keep-ratios to the measured FVS time per band gives about 195 s of FVS plus about 20 s of ISI removed, minus about 45 s of added sparse infill. That is about -2.8 min from extrusion, or about -4.4 min with the travel overhead, against the claimed -3.6 / -6.0. A range of -3 to -6 min is plausible. All of it is planner-based, and this planner overestimated the 4-up plate against Bambu Studio.

There is no FVS/ISI FEATURE block between Z 19.56 and 26.44 (awk), while sparse infill there is 1.79 m (Z 20-24). Mid-height faces are mostly 75-90°. This makes the existing reference pieces at Z 20-28 a valid walls-plus-gyroid control.
GCodeProcessor.cpp:6111-6113 maps erFloatingVerticalShell to erSolidInfill. Its md5 matches the tag download.

recommendation_problems: The percentage uses an outdated denominator. Bambu Studio estimates 57m23s per piece for 4-up without timelapse and 1h00m30s with it (ETAPA_B.md:93-94), not 1h04-1h08. So -3.5 to -6 min is about 6-10%. The savings also come from analisar_gcode's planner, which overestimated the 4-up plate by about 47 min against Bambu Studio (ETAPA_B.md:101). Treat the size of the saving as soft.

The edit recipe starts from the original 3MF plus '...'. That file has wall_generator=classic and default_acceleration=4000, so a test built that way would not match production. Build the test from variantes/Jogos_Vorazes_producao_4pecas.3mf and change only ensure_vertical_shell_thickness. That file already has arachne, 6000, consistent_surface and the 4 instances.

The slicing checks are too tight. 'Z 12-48 ≈ 0 FVS' and '250-330 mm³ remaining' assume the simulation's partial branch is exact. That branch omits the stTop opening and expansion (PrintObject.cpp:1509,1530,1767) and the second clause of the area filter (:2059-2061). An analytic estimate keeps narrow ribbons on 40-48° faces at Z 8-16 and 40-48. Use a looser threshold, for example up to about 450 mm³ remaining.

The risk framing overstates the mechanism. Above about 21° slope, the outside surface is the outer wall in both modes. The removed ribbon only backs the inner wall of the next layers, which then overhangs gyroid by s (at most 0.19 mm). That inner wall also has gyroid touching it in the same layer, as on the near-vertical Z 20-28 band. This supports 'medium-low', but the visual check is still required.

Minor: the minimum-layer-time claim counts 125 layers where the bands hold 175. At Z 4-8 the single-piece layers (minimum about 9.7 s nominal) end up close to 8 s after removal. This does not affect 4-up production.
